title: Protocol-by-String-Concatenation (PROTOCOL_STRING_CONCATENATION)
pattern: Formatting low-level network or transport commands by directly concatenating substrings with delimiter strings without escaping boundaries or using structured command builders.
why_bad: It leads to boundary injection vulnerabilities. If the `payload` contains a delimiter character (e.g., `|`), it will slice the packet prematurely, allowing attackers to inject downstream commands (Command Injection) or cause protocol desynchronization.
detection: Look for occurrences of `format!` or string concatenation (`+`) constructing raw transport command lines containing explicit delimiter characters.
fix: Sanitize and escape input payloads against protocol delimiters, or serialize using structured, length-prefixed protocol definitions.
source: *Michael C. Feathers - Working Effectively with Legacy Code (2004)*, Chapter 19.
